title: UK geothermal register
threshold_note: 45 kWth is the MCS ceiling (MIS 3005) and the Boiler Upgrade Scheme limit. Above it a system sits outside the domestic certification regime and is designed bespoke, so it is a defensible line between 'a building's system' and 'a household's appliance'.

privacy.rule: Tier A sites are named with coordinates because an organisation is not a data subject. Tier B is domestic and is NEVER plotted as a point - only counted by outward code.
privacy.why: A full postcode plus 'has a ground source heat pump' is one lookup from an address: the EPC register is public, searchable by postcode, and records the main heating system. The ICO test is all means reasonably likely to be used, assuming a determined person with a reason to identify. Postcode-only fails that test for a domestic installation.
privacy.tier_b_granularity: outward code (the part before the space, e.g. LL57). Never the full postcode, never a point.

evidence_rule.statement: This register is a LOCATOR, not a STATISTIC.
evidence_rule.detail: It answers where systems are. It must never be used to characterise how the fleet performs. Self-submitted entries carry the same selection bias as any opt-in monitoring sample - people with systems that work submit, people with systems that disappoint do not. No mean SPF, no aggregate performance figure, and nothing here may feed the ECUK-anchored figures elsewhere on this site.
evidence_rule.performance_fields: If performance is ever recorded it is self_reported_spf, and it is displayed per-site, never averaged.

submission.label: Add a system
submission.note: Set url to a live form and the button appears on the panel; leave it null and the box shows the text alone, with no dead link. The form asks only about systems at or above 45 kWth, which are organisations' buildings rather than households, so there is no branch and no special case: site name, operator, full address, capacity, heating / cooling / storage, type (gshp, ates, btes, minewater, deep), loop (open or closed), year commissioned, current status, and a source or a contact to verify against. If a submitter reports a system under 45 kWth, the entry is declined rather than downgraded - see scope. With url null and email set, the button becomes a mailto carrying those fields as the message body: the register can be submitted to without any form infrastructure, at the cost of the sender deleting the prompts. Swap email for a role address such as register@ once one exists - it is a data change here, not a code change.
submission.handling: Submissions land in a private response store, not in this file. Nothing is published until it is checked against a source and committed by hand. Until then an entry is verification: reported.
submission.privacy: Confining the form to 45 kWth and above removes the personal-data question rather than managing it. An organisation is not a data subject, so a named building with an address raises nothing; a household is, and a full postcode plus 'has a ground source heat pump' is one lookup from an address on the public EPC register. Not asking is a property of the form. The only personal data left is the submitter's own contact detail, collected to verify the entry, said so on the form, and never published.

routes.form: For logging a system. Structured fields map onto this schema without re-keying, and the branch above is enforceable in the form itself.
routes.email: For correcting a row. Corrections are conversational, usually arrive with a source attached, and come from operators who want a named person. Use a role address, not a personal one: it is published on a page with traffic and will be scraped.

submission.scope: At or above 45 kWth only. The register does not collect domestic systems at all - not as points, not as counts, not as postcodes. The national domestic base is already counted by MCS registration, which is a census rather than a self-selected sample, so a submitted domestic count would be a worse version of a figure that exists. A sub-45 NON-domestic site (a demonstration rig, a social housing scheme) may be entered by hand for precedent value and appears in the table with meets_threshold: false, but it is never solicited and never plotted.

verification_states.verified: Checked against a primary source. Source URL present. Plotted normally.
verification_states.reported: Submitted via the form, not yet checked. Shown distinctly, or withheld until checked.
verification_states.disputed: Contradicted by another source, or the operator has queried it. Shown with the caveat.

fields.name: the site as it is publicly known
fields.operator: owner or operator; null if unclear
fields.location_precision: address | town | unknown - never give a precise point for a town-level fact
fields.does_cooling: true | false | null  - the field that does not exist anywhere else in UK data
fields.has_storage: true | false | null  - seasonal store (ATES/BTES), not a buffer vessel
fields.status: operating | monitoring | construction | planned | suspended | inoperable | cancelled | never_commissioned | decommissioned | unknown
fields.source_urls: array, at least one for anything marked verified
fields.notes: uncertainty, disputes, anything a reader should weigh
fields.confidence: high | medium | low - how far the sourcing actually supports the row, separate from whether a source exists
fields.meets_threshold: true | false | null - null where no capacity is published, which is most of them
fields.effective_kWth: what it actually delivers, number or null. Differs from nameplate where a system is impaired (Girdwood 180 -> 108) or dead (0). capacity_kWth carries effective where known, nameplate otherwise.
fields.failure_mode: why a system under-delivers or never ran; null where none
fields.designer: designer or installer, null if unknown

sites.name: Colchester Northern Gateway Heat Network
sites.operator: Colchester City Council / Colchester Amphora Energy Ltd
sites.notes: Open-loop groundwater heat pump, one-directional (not ATES): 5 boreholes, 135 m deep, into confined Chalk from c.75 m bgl; 2 abstraction (BH4, BH5) and 3 reinjection (BH1-3), >550 m apart; installed and tested 2018-19. Design: c.18 l/s (c.65 m3/h) abstracted at 13 C, reinjected at 5 C; 800 kW water-source heat pump; 65 C network flow; gas boilers for backup/peak. Design output c.5.5 GWh/yr (c.75% of demand) at full build-out - target, not measured. Status set to planned 22 Nov 2026 (was construction): energy centre installation tendered 2021 (Pinnacle Power) then put on hold; 2023 council panel report says design complete, awaiting confirmation of development build-out; no evidence found of energy centre build, connections or commissioning. 800 kWth corroborated by council and Amphora. No EA permit grid ref found; still town-centre point.

sites.notes: Two GEA ammonia heat pumps, 3 MW each. Boreholes about 150 m. Mine water 15 C in, 8 C return; DH flow 65-80 C. Operational 29 March 2023. Largest of its kind in GB. Sited 22 Nov 2026 at 54°57'52.35"N 1°35'30.30"W, read from Google Earth and supplied by user in chat (underlying source not stated; assumed to be the energy centre); replaces town centroid 54.9526,-1.603. Register capacity (6 MW) kept. Paper's GEC monitoring borehole JC2 (BNG 426286,563523) lies c. 133 m from the plotted point, consistent with it being on the energy centre.

sites.name: Gateshead Mine Water Heat Living Laboratory
sites.notes: RESEARCH/MONITORING ONLY – supplies no heat; status 'monitoring', not plotted (user decision 22 Nov 2026). Mine water monitoring network between the three operating schemes in the Walker mine water block (Gateshead Energy Company, Lanchester Wines Nest Road and Abbotsford Road). MRA-financed. 5 boreholes drilled in two phases, 4 completed (one Bede hole abandoned). Bede site (Bede Primary School grounds), drilled from Mar 2023, data from Jul 2023: High Main BH 55.61 m bgl (BNG 426792,562670); Brass Thill BH 135.61 m bgl (BNG 426781,562670; did not reach Hutton target). Stadium site (Gateshead International Stadium), drilled from May 2024, data from Sep 2024: High Main BH 82.08 m (BNG 427126,562787); Hutton BH 188.97 m (BNG 427129,562785) – c. 54.95898,-1.57790, about 350 m east of the plotted Bede point. Target horizons: High Main and Hutton coal workings, Pennine Middle Coal Measures. Instruments: LTC loggers, vibrating-wire piezometers, thermistors, fibre-optic DTS (Silixa Ltd). Measured geothermal gradient 0.06 °C/m. Drilling contract awarded Mar 2022; officially launched Jan 2025. Driller named in paper acknowledgements as 'DrilCrop Ltd' (read as DrilCorp). Sited 22 Nov 2026 at the Bede site from paper Table 2; replaces town centroid 54.9526,-1.603. Previous Heating=yes corrected to no.

sites.name: Lanchester Wines – Abbotsford Road
sites.operator: Lanchester Wines; O&M by TownRock Energy
sites.notes: Open loop, abstraction–reinjection. 3 abstraction wells (BH1–3, 117/110/123 m) and 3 reinjection wells (BH4–6, c. 155 m), plus 3 observation wells; 6 production wells completed early 2016 after 3 investigation wells in 2015. Abstracts from the unmined Coal Measures Upper Aquifer System; reinjects to the High Main Aquifer System (High Main seam workings and High Main Post sandstone), Felling Colliery. EA abstraction licence NE/023/0006/023, 17 Jul 2018: 49 l/s, 882,000 m³/y. Coal Authority Heat Access Agreement CA11/MHR/0015/N, 25 May 2017. Operating at 20–30 l/s (May 2021), mostly from BH2 alone; abstracted water 11–13 °C. UNDER-DELIVERS: authors estimate >100 l/s needed for the full 2.4 MW, and say flows are less than required for the full design heating load — Effective kWth not published, so capacity left at nameplate. Recurring iron-ochre clogging of the plate heat exchanger (acid cleans 2019–2021). Site: c. 4.5 ha plot north of the A184 Abbotsford Road by Heworth station. Coordinates 54.955 N 1.556 W as published (3 d.p., c. ±60 m), placed on the site. Split 22 Nov 2026 from the single row 'lanchester-wines-mine-water-heat-systems' (3,600 kW combined); the two Lanchester Wines warehouse sites are separate abstraction–reinjection schemes c. 700 m apart. Capacity conflict remains: Banks et al. 2022 and Todd et al. 2026 give 2.4 + 1.2 MW; Gateshead Council describes c. 4 MW across three warehouses; the 2023 Lyell EGC paper says 2.4 and 3 MW. Commissioning year (2015, carried over from the combined row) is NOT supported by either paper — 2015 was the investigation-drilling year — check before publishing. O&M by TownRock Energy (paper co-author).

sites.name: Lanchester Wines – Nest Road
sites.operator: Lanchester Wines; O&M by TownRock Energy
sites.notes: Open loop, abstraction–reinjection. 1 abstraction well (BH04, 131 m) and 1 reinjection well (BH02, 280 m), plus 2 observation wells; 4 wells drilled 2016 (BH03 deepened 2018). Abstracts from the High Main Aquifer System at c. 13 °C (13–14 °C per Todd 2026); reinjects to the Deep Mined Aquifer System (Hutton and Harvey-Beaumont workings). BH04 yields 60–70 l/s, but BH02 reinjection tested only to 40 l/s; operating at c. 40 l/s. Authors estimate >50 l/s needed for the full 1.2 MW. As of May 2021 operating as extended operational testing under a limited-duration EA licence — confirm a full licence before treating as fully commissioned. Site: c. 2.5 ha plot c. 700 m NW of Abbotsford Road. Coordinates 54.959 N 1.564 W as published (3 d.p., c. ±60 m), placed on the site. Split 22 Nov 2026 from the single row 'lanchester-wines-mine-water-heat-systems' (3,600 kW combined); the two Lanchester Wines warehouse sites are separate abstraction–reinjection schemes c. 700 m apart. Capacity conflict remains: Banks et al. 2022 and Todd et al. 2026 give 2.4 + 1.2 MW; Gateshead Council describes c. 4 MW across three warehouses; the 2023 Lyell EGC paper says 2.4 and 3 MW. Commissioning year (2015, carried over from the combined row) is NOT supported by either paper — 2015 was the investigation-drilling year — check before publishing. O&M by TownRock Energy (paper co-author).

sites.name: AstraZeneca Discovery Centre (DISC), Cambridge Biomedical Campus
sites.notes: 174 closed-loop boreholes serving a ground source heat pump with hybrid cooling towers, heating and cooling a laboratory building on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus. Opened November 2021; construction from 2015 (Skanska to 2018, then Mace). BREEAM Excellent for design and construction. Described by the architects as thought to be the UK’s largest renewable-heat-certified ground source system, which is a claim rather than a measured ranking. | NO CAPACITY PUBLISHED. No kWth, borehole depth or array spacing is given in any source found, so capacity_kWth is null and meets_threshold is set true on the array size alone. An Ofgem non-domestic RHI accreditation would carry the rated capacity if the RHI register can be reached. | DISCREPANCIES. Cooling towers: four in the 2021 press release and the architects’ account, five in AstraZeneca’s own 2024 sustainability article. Floor area: 19,000-19,905 m² is the laboratory element; the building as a whole is about 70,000 m², so the smaller figure should not be quoted as the served area. | THE "TWO HOUSEHOLDS" CLAIM IS NOT SUPPORTED. A widely shared figure puts the building’s carbon footprint at that of two UK households; no source found states it, and it is not plausible for a 24/7 laboratory of this size. The published claim is different and is about savings, not footprint: the heat pump "will save enough energy to power 2,500 homes" (AstraZeneca, 2021). Treated as unsubstantiated pending a primary source. | STORAGE. Sources say the boreholes "store and provide" geothermal energy, but nothing describes a designed seasonal store, and the hybrid cooling towers imply surplus heat is rejected rather than banked. has_storage left null rather than recorded as BTES. | SITING UNVERIFIED. Placed 23 Nov 2026 from the published postal address (1 Francis Crick Avenue, Cambridge CB2 0AA) without geocoder access in this session - no source gives coordinates. Flagged for a Google Earth check before the point is trusted at address precision.

tier_b.note: NOT COLLECTED. Reserved in the schema and deliberately left empty. Domestic systems under 45 kWth are counted nationally by MCS registration, which is a census; an opt-in submission count would be a self-selected subset of the same population and could not be used as a statistic under evidence_rule anyway. If domestic context is ever shown on the panel it is quoted from MCS, with its date, and not assembled here.

source_quality_note: GSNI’s 2021 summary for the Geological Advisory Committee is the only public source naming NI installations, and it is demonstrably wrong about at least two of the six it lists: Royal Victoria Hospital never operated, and the Lyric is cooling-only. Riddel Hall is likewise recorded there as heating and cooling when it is heating and DHW. No NI entry should rest on GSNI alone.
inclusion_rule: Systems that exist as hardware. A scheme enters the register when plant or boreholes were installed, whatever happened to it afterwards - so cancelled, never-commissioned, suspended and decommissioned systems stay in, and stay off the map. Feasibility studies, proposals and schemes that were only ever claimed are NOT entries, however well sourced the claim: a register of intentions is not a register. Where a published list names a system that was never built, the correction is recorded in superseded_claims below rather than as a row here.

superseded_claims.note: Claims in published sources that this register does not carry, and why. These are not systems and are never counted, mapped or totalled - they exist so that a correction to a public list can be cited rather than asserted.
